title: HelperSSHForwardedTCPIPEvent
description: The announcement that a connection arrived on a listener the coordinator asked for. It is an announcement and not a result because nobody here asked: the coordinator holds a listener, and the connection is the far side's act — so there is no request to answer, and this notification is the only place the channel's id can come from. Ordering is what makes that sufficient: it rides the same wire as the data frames, and the helper writes it under the writer mutex it writes the first byte with (nocx-50w7p.8).

forward.description: The listener the connection arrived on. An id the coordinator does not hold is answered by closing the channel: the announcement both creates and names the stream, so there is no window to park one in.

channel.description: The channel the connection's bytes are keyed by — an ORDINARY channel from here on: the same data frames, the same close, the same end-of-stream notification as a channel an open produced.

peer.description: The accepted connection's remote address as the far side reported it, for the log and for the local end's RemoteAddr. It is somebody else's machine's claim and never an authentication: the lifecycle capability is what authenticates a candidate connection, and this is deliberately not a second, weaker way to.
